solutionData.generation_method: Iterated Local Search (ILS) with FFT-based evaluation and multiple restarts.

details.objective_function: Minimizing max|P(z)| on the unit circle (equivalent to minimizing peak-to-RMS ratio as RMS is constant sqrt(N)).
details.evaluation_method: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for polynomial evaluation on 2^17 = 131072 evenly spaced points on the unit circle. This provides a more accurate and efficient peak calculation than direct summation for a large number of points.
details.local_search_strategy: Iterative single-coefficient flip. For a given polynomial, iterate through each coefficient. If flipping a coefficient improves the peak value, accept the flip and restart the iteration from the beginning. Continue until a full pass over all coefficients yields no improvement.
details.perturbation_strategy: After reaching a local optimum, randomly flip 5-10 coefficients to jump out of the local minimum and explore a new region of the search space.
details.restarts: Multiple independent runs (restarts) of the ILS algorithm were performed with different initial random polynomials to increase the chance of finding a global optimum.
details.symmetries_considered: No explicit symmetry constraints were enforced during the search, but the algorithm is free to discover symmetric or anti-symmetric solutions if they are optimal.
details.computational_notes: The use of FFT significantly speeds up the evaluation of the objective function, allowing for a much deeper search within a reasonable timeframe. The search was run for several hours across multiple CPU cores.
